money_at_stake.rationale: The deal is reported with two large, mutually corroborating dollar figures on top of a 65+ billion barrel reserve base across 17 fields: 'nearly $100 billion' in private investment attributed to Secretary of State Rubio and 'over $209 billion' in tax revenue for the Venezuelan government attributed to Vice President Rodriguez, both reported by CBS News the same day the deal was announced. Euronews independently confirms the 17-field, 65-billion-barrel scope. A separate CBS passage attributes to a U.S. official the grant of a 100-year concession over those same 65 billion barrels. Discovery Alert independently frames the investment side as 'over $100 billion in investment commitments... required to commercialise Orinoco Belt extra-heavy crude,' consistent with the CBS figure, alongside a projected incremental output of 1-2 million barrels per day. Investment plus tax revenue together clear $300B across the reporting, comfortably above the GT_100B floor, so the band is set there without treating either single number as precise: no outlet fetched this run gives a phased public breakdown, and the deal's own duration is described only as a 100-year concession, so this is sized as an order-of-magnitude band over the life of the arrangement, not a point estimate or an annualized figure. Note on this pass: the prior draft also asserted a Lake Maracaibo light-crude component alongside the Orinoco Belt extra-heavy crude and a direct Euronews citation for the 100-year term; neither survived fetching the cited page (Euronews states 17 fields and 65bn barrels but nothing about concession length or crude-type split), so both are dropped from this rationale and the 100-year fact is now cited to CBS instead, where it is actually stated.

public_reach.rationale: The equity in the actual vehicle this occurrence creates is not listed anywhere: CBS reports the new joint venture is 55% US government, split between equity and the right to buy oil at cost, and describes the venture as a joint project of the US government and one private operator, so the remaining share is 45% by arithmetic (CBS never states 45% itself). That share belongs to 'an experienced private operator in Venezuela' that CBS says remains unnamed: 'It's not clear which private companies will be involved.' PDVSA, Venezuela's fully state-owned oil company, is the counterparty handing over the fields per the same reporting. That is the state-plus-private-dominated shape the 15-anchor describes almost exactly. Not scored at the floor because a real, separately-confirmed listed layer exists alongside it: Yahoo Finance reports Chevron (NYSE: CVX) is nearing deals to invest billions of dollars in Venezuela's oil fields, expanding on agreements it signed in April to broaden its Orinoco Belt operations, and CBS names Repsol and Eni as the only other foreign majors with a standing Venezuelan presence. None of the three is confirmed as the unnamed 45% private-operator partner in the government-to-government deal itself. Note on this pass: the Yahoo Finance Chevron piece was published a day before this deal was announced and never mentions it, the 65-billion-barrel reserve figure, or any US government joint venture, so the comparison drawn in the prior draft's claim overstated what that specific article says; the claim below is trimmed to only what it actually states. Chevron's exposure here is parallel and thematic (same country, same sector) rather than a stake in this specific transaction, which is why this sits well below the 40 mixed-reach anchor rather than at it.

capture_odds.rationale: Sovereign and regulatory reversal risk here is demonstrated, not hypothetical: the prior US-Venezuela oil concession arrangement, tracing to a Nov. 26, 2022 Biden-era authorization letting Chevron resume operations, was ordered terminated by President Trump as of the following March 1st renewal option, calling it 'ineffective and unmet,' roughly eighteen months before this new deal was announced, under the same administration now granting a fresh 100-year concession (Yahoo News, February 2025). That is the precise failure mode the 15-anchor names: a return that can be revoked or renegotiated by policy rather than sticking as profit for whoever holds it. Layered on top, the reserve base is mostly extra-heavy Orinoco Belt crude, which trades at a structural quality discount to benchmark grades, and energy analysts on the record (Rystad Energy's Claudio Galimberti, GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan, both quoted by Time) describe years of drilling and infrastructure build-out before any output materializes. Not scored at the floor because the deal structure gives its equity holders (the US government and the still-unnamed private operator, not public shareholders) a favorable right to buy oil at cost, and any of the confirmed listed majors (Chevron, Repsol, Eni) that do participate in the broader sector reopening bring real negotiating leverage as scarce, technically-qualified operators in a country that needs outside capital and expertise.

timing_fit.rationale: Measured from this occurrence's own anchor_date (2026-08-29; the candidate record carries no separate window, so the 2-5 year horizon runs to roughly 2028-2031), the dated reporting places most of the money outside that window rather than inside it. Discovery Alert states plainly that the incremental 1-2 million barrel per day output potential is 'a late 2020s to early 2030s story, contingent on sustained capital deployment and successful reconstruction of the Orinoco Belt's extra-heavy crude infrastructure.' Energy analysts quoted by name the same week (Time) say the practical effect is 'several quarters and, in quite a few cases, years' out, 'mostly in the medium-long term.' Unlike a signed, under-construction capex program, this deal has not yet named its private-sector counterparty, so committed investment has not visibly started; the vehicle itself carries 100-year rights per a State Department official quoted by Time, underscoring that this is a multi-decade structure whose spend only partially overlaps a 2-5 year window rather than sitting inside it. Not scored at the floor because a real production ramp is explicitly dated to begin before the window closes (late 2020s), just not concentrated inside it. Note on this pass: the prior draft's Discovery Alert claim also asserted that officials gave 'no public timeline' for the investment; that clause is not stated on the fetched page, so it is dropped here.
